Manus to resume independent operations in unwind of Meta deal
article:
(Aug 11): The Chinese-founded artificial intelligence startup Manus said it would soon resume operating as an independent company, the latest step in efforts to unwind its purchase by Meta Platforms Inc after government authorities in China blocked the transaction.

In a message to users posted Tuesday, Manus said that some customers’ accounts may be impacted and outlined a series of steps it was taking to ensure a smooth transition. It warned that some user data may be at risk of being deleted and offered data-protection tools.

“Manus will soon return to operating as an independent company, which will see us continue to serve our millions of users around the world,” the company said. “This is part of our separation from Meta; we must take this step to comply with regulatory requirements in specific parts of the world.”

China moved in April to block Meta’s US$2 billion takeover of the Manus, a firm that was founded in China but had moved to Singapore in 2025 as it made gains in agent-driven AI. Authorities in Beijing ordered the deal’s cancellation amid growing criticism that China was at risk of losing valuable technology to a geopolitical rival.

The decision, outlined in a brief statement from the National Development and Reform Commission, marked a rare move to reverse an already completed transaction. It followed a directive barring major tech firms, including ByteDance Ltd and Moonshot, from taking American capital without approval and a clampdown on offshore Chinese companies seeking to list in Hong Kong.

Taken together, the moves represented a warning to other Chinese technology startups that they should think twice before selling stakes or transferring sensitive technology to US investors. The measures are taking effect as AI firms in China, including Moonshot and DeepSeek, continue to gain ground on their Silicon Valley rivals with chatbots that perform near levels of systems from OpenAI and Anthropic PBC.

See also: White House lifts ban on TikTok from US government devices

Manus and Meta completed their operational split in May and halted data-sharing between the two companies, Bloomberg News previously reported. Manus’ founders have explored raising about US$1 billion to fund a buyback as part of their effort to meet Chinese government demands to unwind its combination with Meta.

Manus said in its message to users Tuesday that the company was preparing a new set of features that will add to the capabilities of its AI agents, without elaborating. “We look forward to continuing to serve and delight you in this next chapter,” it said.

title: White House lifts ban on TikTok from US government devices
article:
(Aug 11): The Trump administration has lifted restrictions on the use of TikTok on federal government devices, after finding that the popular social media app no longer poses a national security threat following the shift of its US operations to American investors.

In a memo dated Monday, the White House Office of Management and Budget rescinded a 2023 directive barring use of the video-sharing service on government equipment over concerns that TikTok’s then-Chinese ownership represented a security risk. The memo follows a written opinion last month from the Justice Department that concluded TikTok no longer qualified as a “covered application” under a law passed in 2022 that had barred its use on federal platforms.

The decision follows the completion in January of a deal to transfer control of the app’s US business from its Chinese parent ByteDance Ltd to a consortium of American firms led by Oracle Corp and private equity firm Silver Lake Management LLC. Orchestrated by US President Donald Trump, the deal was designed to spare the app from a US ban under a 2024 law sparked by fears that TikTok and ByteDance could share information on US users with Chinese authorities.

The Justice Department’s opinion said that the current version of TikTok functions independently of ByteDance and is now majority owned by US investors. Under its new ownership, the app “has revised the content recommendation algorithm and cybersecurity programme originally developed by ByteDance to insulate federal government information against the concerning security features that initially motivated the prohibition”.

The TikTok sale followed a yearlong tug-of-war over US national security concerns raised by the app’s Chinese connections. TikTok and the government in Beijing have rejected claims by US policymakers that users’ data could be exploited and that the app could be used by China to push certain narratives or sow disinformation.

Trump has praised TikTok and credited the app with helping him win the 2024 election and he expressed gratitude to Chinese leader Xi Jinping for helping clear the way for approval of the sale.

See also: China hits back at US with tighter drone export curbs, sanctions

title: Tencent’s WorkBuddy sparks AI turnaround hopes after stock rout
article:
(Aug 11): Tencent Holdings Ltd’s early success with WorkBuddy may give the Chinese Internet giant a chance to catch up after lagging peers in the artificial intelligence race for the past few years.

A flood of users has made WorkBuddy China’s most popular AI workplace assistant, just months after its launch. Investors keenly await any data on the desktop agent that Tencent may release along with its earnings report on Wednesday.

Concrete signs of AI traction could become a catalyst for its stock, which has trailed the massive gains in upstart pure-plays like Z.AI Co. Tencent’s valuation remains near a record low, despite a recent small rebound amid outflows from tech hardware shares in South Korea and Taiwan.

“If they start to disclose encouraging metrics on WorkBuddy, I think that will help change people’s perception about Tencent,” said Jiong Shao, a Barclays Capital Inc analyst in New York. “Tencent became No. 1 in our picks recently for the first time in five years because we think in the longer term they have a bigger chance to win.”

WorkBuddy has been one of the most successful new products launched by Tencent in March to tap into the AI usership frenzy unleashed by OpenClaw. As of June, the agent had attracted 20.97 million monthly visits, beating ByteDance Ltd’s Trae and Alibaba Group Holding Ltd’s QoderWork, according to a local media report from 36kr that cited data provider Analysys.

See also: Singapore-based data centre operator is said to confidentially file for US$5 bil IPO in US

Office agents are becoming a hot AI battleground globally, with the broad white-collar workforce a much larger potential market than coders. Tencent is reportedly prioritising WorkBuddy as competition heats up in China, with the likes of Baidu Inc and MoonShot AI also rolling out workplace assistants.

“If we were to find one thing within Tencent’s AI strategy that’s worth highlighting, I think WorkBuddy is the go-to for investors,” said Morningstar Inc senior equity analyst Ivan Su. He sees the agent’s integration into the popular WeChat app making it stickier and harder to replace than rivals’ products.

Investors will also be closely watching the company’s spending plans in its upcoming results and the impact on profits. Tencent’s capital expenditure is expected to be similar to Alibaba’s this year. For the June quarter, Tencent is projected to post revenue growth of nearly 10% and a profit increase of 5%.

See also: From black box to glass box: Rethinking AI in financial operations

Tencent shares fell as much as 2.5% on Tuesday, trimming their rebound from a June low to around 14%. The stock is down 22% for the year, compared with the Hang Seng Tech Index’s 12% drop.

China’s largest company with a market value of US$557 billion, Tencent has a vast business empire from social networks to games, e-commerce and payments. Some see its size combined with the ubiquity of its products as giving it a leg up in the AI arena.

“Tencent may be the only company in the whole world that can have a very good general-purpose AI agent,” said Barclays Capital’s Shao. The company’s “strategic resource allocation to WorkBuddy has given it a competitive advantage over rivals”.

title: Delfi reports 5.4% y-o-y rise in patmi to US$12.9 mil for 1HFY2026, declares 1.05 US cents interim dividend
article:
For 1HFY2026 ended June 30, confectionary company Delfi has reported a 5.4% climb in patmi to US$12.9 ($16.5) million on revenue of US$266.6 million which is a 2.7% y-o-y increase. On a constant currency basis, the patmi increase would be 9.4% and the revenue increase, 2.9%.

Gross profit declined by 4.1% y-o-y to US$68.5 million, weighed down by cost of sales which increased by 5.3% to slightly above US$198 million. The gross profit margin was 25.7%, a 180 basis points decline from 1HFY2025.

On a segmental basis, sales for its own brands rose 13.3% y-o-y to US$172.9 million, supported by a “steady” growth trajectory in Indonesia, the Philippines and Malaysia. Meanwhile, overall agency brands sales declined 12.4% y-o-y to US$93.7 million. This reflected the 3Q2025 strategic exit from an agency account, particularly in Indonesia. Excluding the terminated account, sales for the agency brands business grew 29% y-o-y.

As at June 30, Delfi held cash of around US$63.3 million with US$20.3 million in borrowings. The company generated net operating cash flow of US$14.0 million which the company says provides the financial flexibility to “comfortably” fund strategic capital investment while continuing to return value to shareholders.

Delfi has declared a 1.05 US cents dividend payable on Sept 11. This represents a 50% payout ratio of patmi.

CEO John Chuang says: “Our 1H 2026 performance demonstrates the continued strength of our Own Brands, highlighting the underlying demand of our key brands even as we navigated a challenging cost environment. By pairing top-line growth with disciplined cash management, we maintain a stable financial foundation to navigate current market challenges and continue delivering shareholder value.”

See also: OKP Holdings reports 43.8% y-o-y increase in earnings for 1HFY2026, declares special interim dividend of 0.6 cents

Shares in Delfi closed 0.5 cents or 0.6% lower to 86 cents on Aug 11.

title: Eneco Energy to acquire 15 Gul Way for $24.2 mil
article:
Eneco Energy (SGX:R14 ) announced that its wholly-owned subsidiary, Richland Global Pte Ltd, has entered into a sale and purchase agreement to acquire a JTC industrial property located at 15 Gul Way for $24.2 million.

The industrial property has a total land area of around 203,267 square feet and comprises a gross floor area of 284,384 square feet, together with an on-site dormitory that can accommodate up to 199 personnel.

Eneco Energy explains that the proposed acquisition will help enhance its logistics capabilities with greater operational flexibility and efficiency and will help support future business expansion of its logistic division.

In addition, Eneco Energy expects the on-site dormitory will help in reducing its recurring employee accommodation costs.

“Together with our ongoing strategic initiatives across the business, we believe this property acquisition will enhance the group's competitive position, strengthen our long-term growth platform, and create sustainable value for our stakeholders,” says Ang Jun Long, executive director of Eneco Energy.

Shares of Eneco Energy closed unchanged at 0.8 cents on Aug 11.

title: Yangzijiang Maritime reports 29.4% y-o-y decline in patmi to US$44.9 mil for 1HFY2026
article:
For 1HFY2026 ended June 30, Yangzijiang (YZJ) Maritime Development has reported a 29.4% decline in patmi to US$44.9 ($57.5) million, on total income of US$81.6 million, which is 49.3% higher y-o-y.

Profit before tax declined 30.6% y-o-y to US$50.2 million. The weaker earnings performance is attributed to a 186% y-o-y increase in maritime asset operating expenses to US$26.9 million and less earnings from joint ventures and associates by 52.1% to US$6.97 million. The company also saw a currency revaluation loss on financial assets which amounted to US$5.6 million in contrast to a gain of US$16.1 million in 1HFY2025.

The growth in total income is attributed to the strong performance and strategic expansion of its core maritime business. YZJ Maritime adds that the higher income reflects its focus on building a “resilient, high-quality” earnings base.

While the company acknowledges the higher operating costs arising from maritime business expansion, it says this strengthens its ability to harness greater value creation opportunities through strategic asset monetisation and resale opportunities with a growing pipeline of newbuild maritime assets.

On a segmental basis, income from the maritime business increased by 70% to US$51.7 million. This was driven mainly by higher income from maritime fund assets and reflected the expanded maritime fund asset portfolio with increased newbuilds.

Under cash management, the income jumped 120% or to US$14.4 million, mainly due to net gains in the fair value of financial assets and liabilities as a result of favourable mark to market movements. This was, however, partially offset by lower interest income earned from reduced treasury cash balances.

See also: SingLand’s patmi surges 90% y-o-y in 1HFY2026, S’pore portfolio valuation rises 1.3% h-o-h

For the other non-maritime investments segment, income dipped by 12.3% to US$15.5 million , mainly due to lower interest income.

Reflecting the strategic deployment of cash into its core maritime business, the balance sheet saw a rebalancing of the asset mix from current to non-current assets. The company held cash and equivalents of US$238 million without any bank borrowings as at June 30. NAV increased by around 2% to 47.47 US cents.

Outlook-wise, the company notes that the maritime industry is an “indispensable cornerstone” of global economic development, serving as the “lifeblood” of international trade, commerce, and connectivity.

See also: MoneyMax reports 73.7% y-o-y surge in net profit to record $52.5 mil for 1HFY2026

It aims to capitalise on the macro opportunities brought on by the structural shifts within the maritime industry, which are driven by tighter capital conditions in the Western capital markets and accelerating decarbonisation requirements by the International Maritime Organization (IMO), among others.

CEO Ren Yuanlin says that the company has been “building a stronger foundation’ by expanding its maritime business and pipeline of newbuild vessel orders since its November listing. He adds: “Given the two to three year shipbuilding cycle, there is a natural transition period before our maritime investments are realised, during which upfront capital commitments and expenses are required. Underpinned by deep maritime expertise and established global network, our strategy of entering into sale contracts early enables us to lock in reasonable capital gain returns, while providing earnings visibility ahead as the vessels are progressively delivered accordingly.

“Supported by a disciplined capital recycling strategy and a strong balance sheet, we aim to expand both our recurring operating income base and capital gains returns ahead, creating long-term value for our shareholders.”

Shares in YZJ Maritime closed 2.5 cents or 4% higher to 64 cents on Aug 11.

title: Thailand preparing to use military ties as leverage in US talks
article:
(Aug 11): Thailand plans to warn the Trump administration that steep US tariffs could force it to scale back military cooperation, including the Cobra Gold exercises that anchor one of America’s oldest security alliances in Asia, according to an official familiar with the matter.

The Thai government intends to include the position in a counterproposal as reciprocal-trade negotiations resume later this month, the official said, speaking on condition of anonymity because the discussions are private. While the provision will be broadly worded, Thailand could reconsider its participation in joint military activities if higher tariffs inflict significant economic damage, the official said.

Thailand, which recorded a US$51.4 billion trade surplus with the US last year, is among dozens of nations seeking better trade terms after Washington imposed a 12.5% tariff on most exports under Section 301, a US trade law used to address what it considers unfair trading practices. As the Trump administration expands investigations into manufacturing overcapacity, Bangkok has offered to eliminate tariffs and adopt US standards for imports of beef, lamb and alcoholic beverages.

The proposal would mark a rare attempt by Thailand to invoke its decades-old security partnership with Washington in negotiations otherwise focused on trade. Thailand is one of only two US treaty allies in Southeast Asia, alongside the Philippines, and the alliance has long underpinned American military engagement in mainland Southeast Asia.

Defence Ministry spokesman Surasant Kongsiri said he was unable to verify or confirm the proposal. “If anything, negotiations are more likely to focus on enhancing cooperation,” he said.

The spokesman for Thailand’s armed forces did not respond to a call seeking comments. The Thai Commerce Ministry and the Pentagon didn’t immediately respond to separate emailed requests for comment.

See also: Iran says Hormuz talks underway after Trump calls off strikes

Thai officials have increasingly highlighted the broader relationship in arguing for better trade terms. Commerce Minister Suphajee Suthumpun last month said Thailand deserved more favorable treatment because of the countries’ strategic alliance, the Treaty of Amity and Thai investment in the US.

She described the negotiations as a whole-of-government effort involving the foreign and defence ministries as well as business groups. The government is seeking to keep the tariff rate at no higher than the 19% discussed under an earlier framework. Thailand has also pledged to accelerate legislation banning imports of goods made with forced labour in an effort to address US concerns.

The Thai-US alliance is one of Washington’s oldest in Asia and has long provided the US military with a strategic foothold in a region where China has expanded its influence. Thailand and the US co-host Cobra Gold, a military exercise the US describes as the largest annual multinational drill of its sort in mainland Asia. Last year’s exercise drew about 8,000 personnel from 30 countries.

See also: Euro-area inflation strengthens as US-Iran strikes boost oil

The two countries’ military cooperation has weathered political tensions before. Washington scaled back Cobra Gold and suspended several military engagements after Thailand’s 2014 coup before gradually rebuilding defence ties.

The Pentagon has publicly emphasised the strength of the alliance. During a visit to Bangkok last week, Undersecretary of Defense Elbridge Colby said he and Thai Permanent Secretary for Defense General Tharapong Malakam had reaffirmed “the renewed strength of the US-Thai alliance”.

title: US small-business optimism rises to an almost one-year high
article:
(Aug 11): US small-business optimism rose in July to the highest level in almost a year as firms ramped up hiring plans and inflation pressures eased.

The National Federation of Independent Business index increased 2.4 points to 99.8, the highest level since August 2025. Eight of the 10 components that make up the gauge improved and two declined.

The net share of US small businesses planning to add jobs jumped to the highest level since October 2022 while the share planning to make capital outlays in the months ahead advanced to the strongest reading since the end of 2024.

Concerns around inflation softened. Reports of inflation as the most important problem for business owners fell for the first time this year. The net share of firms that reported raising prices fell for the first time since February, just before the US and Israel military strikes on Iran sent oil prices higher. A smaller share of businesses are planning price increases in the coming months.

Businesses are investing and expanding despite uncertainty that is likely related to the war with Iran.

See also: Trump says rates should drop but it’s not entirely up to Warsh

“Although uncertainty is currently elevated, Main Street anticipates that business conditions will continue to improve,” NFIB chief economist Bill Dunkelberg said in a statement.

title: MoneyMax reports 73.7% y-o-y surge in net profit to record $52.5 mil for 1HFY2026
article:
For 1HFY2026 ended June 30, pawnbroker and microfinancier MoneyMax Financial Services reported a 73.7% increase in net profit to $52.5 million on revenue of $325.7 million, which was higher y-o-y by 34.1%. An interim dividend of 0.25 cents has been declared.

The improved result was attributed to a “strong” performance of the company’s core business segments. Higher interest income from an “expanding” pawnbroking portfolio contributed to a 60.1% y-o-y increase in revenue for pawnbroking to $69.2 million, while more sales supported revenue growth of 30.6% y-o-y to $245 million for the retail and trading of gold and luxury items.

Year-to-date, MoneyMax added 26 new stores across Singapore and Malaysia to bring the total number of stores to 139. The issuer also transferred its listing to the SGX Mainboard from the Catalist board.

In conjunction with its listing transfer, MoneyMax successfully raised gross proceeds of $44.3 million with the placement of 53 million new shares. The capital raising boosted the firm’s war chest to support expansion initiatives, resilient pawnbroking demand and a growing customer base.

CEO Lim Yong Guan says that the company’s first-half performance demonstrates the “strength and resilience” of MoneyMax’s “diversified” business model.

“As we continue to expand our footprint across Singapore and Malaysia, we remain focused on investing in innovation, enhancing customer experience and maintaining prudent capital management,” adds Lim. “While the retail and trading of gold segment may face near-term softness amid cautious consumer sentiment and broader macroeconomic uncertainties, our established market position and resilient customer demand give us confidence in navigating these conditions.”

See also: Frasers Property’s net gearing falls slightly to 93.6% in 3QFY2026

Shares in MoneyMax closed 0.5 cents or 0.6% higher at 86 cents on Aug 11.
